newsitem.title: USA: US Treasury mulls basket commerce limit on banks.
newsitem.headline: US Treasury mulls basket commerce limit on banks.

text.p: With the debate over financial services reform caught up in a controversy over mixing banking and commerce, the Clinton administration is mulling a compromise approach, a senior Treasury Department official said on Wednesday.
Under Secretary of the Treasury John Hawke said the administration is considering allowing financial companies to engage in a limited amount, or "basket," of commercial activity.
"There's a lot to recommend itself in that approach," he told a New York Bankers Association meeting here.

Hawke said a bill introduced by Rep. Marge Roukema, Republican of New Jersey, and Rep. Bruce Vento, Democrat of Minnesota, that would cap non-financial activity at 25 percent of a financial firm's business "has a lot of appeal."

House Banking Committee chairman Jim Leach and other opponents have charged that allowing unlimited combinations between banks and commercial firms would reduce competition and result in massive conglomeration in the U.S. economy.
Hawke said a basket approach, capped at 25 percent or possibly a lesser amount, would give "substantial protection" against mergers of large banks and large commercial firms.

Insurance companies, thrifts and securities firms, which have been allowed to own non-financial businesses, strongly favor legislation that would allow them to own banks without having to give up their commercial interests.
Hawke said the basket approach would give "reasonable comfort and reasonable leeway" to such firms.

The administration is still working on its own financial sector mnodernization plan, Hawke said. Of the basket approach, Hawke said "we're going to be looking very closely at that as we put the final touches on our legislation."

The administration expects to release its plan at the end of March, Hawke said. But he declined to give detailed information about the proposal. "There are some elements yet to be resolved internally," he said.

Earlier on Wednesday, Leach discussed the basket approach at a House subcommittee hearing. While still opposed to the mixing of banking and commerce, Leach made specific suggestions about how a basket approach might be structured.
